# Vendored siteone-crawler binary

- Upstream: https://github.com/janreges/siteone-crawler (MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023-2026 Ján Regeš — see `LICENSE` in this directory).
- Built locally in this environment from the full upstream source tree (already present at `/home/user/janreges/siteone-crawler` in this sandbox) with `cargo build --release` on the pinned toolchain the repo specifies (`rust-toolchain.toml` → Rust 1.96.0), because `github.com` release-asset downloads were not reachable from this sandbox at the time (`api.github.com` returns 200, but the repo itself was not attached/authorized for this session and release asset hosts such as `objects.githubusercontent.com` returned 404 through the network proxy). Building from source (option (b) in the task spec) was therefore used instead of downloading a prebuilt release binary (option (a)).
- Binary: `siteone-crawler` (ELF 64-bit x86_64, ~39 MB, ships with the default `browser` Cargo feature enabled, i.e. it supports `--browser`/Chromium rendering if a Chromium-family browser is available on the host — none was available in this sandbox, see docs/INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- Version reported by the binary: `2.7.0.20260925-dev`.
- This ~39 MB binary is committed as a vendored build artifact for now. It is **not** optimized for Docker layer caching or image size — that is a later-phase concern, flagged explicitly here per the task instructions. A production Dockerfile should instead build this binary in a dedicated build stage (or download a pinned upstream release) rather than copying it from source control, to keep the app repo's git history small.
